I'll read the batch-6 notes, the partial script, and the CIS results so the revision matches what already ran.Paste 1 already landed and the SSH-self stop fired. I'll re-check live ufw and sysctl state, then revise the script so it skips finished steps and still blocks lockout.`ufw.conf` is already `ENABLED=yes`, `log_martians` is 1, and the rollback timer is inactive. The script will re-check as root, skip finished steps, and only arm the timer if it still has to enable ufw.## Detail

Batch 6’s next run is `docs/cis-fix/batch-6.sh`. Paste 1 in `docs/cis-fix/batch-6.md` stays the record of the `log_martians` change. The old Paste 2 fence is not the next paste.

A read-only SSH check at 23:39 UTC found Johnny further along than that write-up. `ufw.service` is enabled and active. `/etc/ufw/ufw.conf` is `ENABLED=yes` (mtime 23:03 UTC, same minute as `/etc/ufw/user.rules`). Input, output, and forward policies are still DROP, ACCEPT, and DROP, with `IPV6=yes`. Both `log_martians` values are 1, the ufw sysctl lines are commented, and `60-johnny-cis-network.conf` has both `= 1` keys. `johnny-ufw-rollback.timer` is inactive. Two established SSH sessions are up: local `192.168.50.152:22`, peer `192.168.50.223` on both. Non-root `ufw status` and `ufw show added` fail, and `user.rules` is mode `0640`, so this session could not see whether the eno3 SSH allow is loaded. The script checks that as root.

`sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-6.sh` runs PASTE 1 only (`# RUNS IN: SSH`). It prints `STATE`, then skips work already done. The SSH allow is added only if missing, and `SSH-RULE-OK` is required before `ufw default deny incoming` or `ufw --force enable`. If `ufw status` is already `Status: active`, it prints `SKIP-enable` and does not arm a timer. If ufw is inactive, it arms `systemd-run --unit=johnny-ufw-rollback --on-active=5min /usr/sbin/ufw --force disable` and only then enables. It then tells AJ to open a new SSH session from aj-rock-box and, only after that shell is up, run `sudo systemctl stop johnny-ufw-rollback.timer`. A peer address of `192.168.50.152` is `NOTE-ssh-self`. It is not a stop. The script ends with `=== VERIFY ===` and `OK-batch-6`.

PASTE 2 (`# RUNS IN: KVM`) runs only as `sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-6.sh 2`. It disables ufw and stops the timer. Full file restore is `## Rollback` in `docs/cis-fix/batch-6.md`. `bash -n` on the script printed `SYNTAX-OK`.

Claude reviews `docs/cis-fix/batch-6.sh` before AJ copies it. After that review, from the repo:

```bash
scp docs/cis-fix/batch-6.sh aj@192.168.50.152:cis-audit/batch-6.sh
```

On Johnny, from the existing SSH session:

```bash
sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-6.sh
```

If that run prints `SKIP-enable` and `OK-batch-6`, ufw was already active and this run did not arm the timer. Send the output. If it prints `ROLLBACK-ARMED`, open a new SSH session from aj-rock-box before stopping the timer. If that new session fails, at the KVM console:

```bash
sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-6.sh 2
```

## Relay

Batch 6 next run is `docs/cis-fix/batch-6.sh` PASTE 1 (`sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-6.sh`), not the rev 6 Paste 2 fence. Live read 23:39 UTC: `ENABLED=yes`, ufw.service active, log_martians 1/1, timer inactive, two SSH peers `.223`. Non-root could not read `ufw status` or `user.rules`. Script skips finished steps, requires `SSH-RULE-OK` before default deny or enable, arms `johnny-ufw-rollback` (5 min `ufw --force disable`) only if it enables, then AJ cancels from a new aj-rock-box shell with `sudo systemctl stop johnny-ufw-rollback.timer`. KVM lockout is `sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-6.sh 2`. Please review the `.sh` before AJ scp’s it.

## Outline

- Script is the next run; history fences stay in the markdown
- Live state: ufw conf enabled, martians already 1, timer off, SSH still up from `.223`
- Root-only checks still needed for the allow rule and `ufw status`
- PASTE 1 skips done work, verifies the eno3 SSH allow, then enables only if inactive
- Five-minute auto-disable is armed only on that enable path
- PASTE 2 is KVM-only; full undo is `## Rollback`
- Claude reviews the script, then AJ scp’s and runs it
